introduction_markdown:

Answer ALL the SIX questions in this booklet. The mark allocation is indicated for each question. Each question carries 20 marks. Verify that this booklet contains six questions, no questions are repeated and there are no blank pages; inform the invigilator in case the booklet contains fewer than six questions, questions are repeated or there are blank pages, so that the booklet may be changed. Blank spaces in the question booklet may be used for rough work. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. questions.enonce_markdown:
Three different reactions of 2-iodopropane are shown below:

![fig-1](gce-al-chemistry-2021-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_6_fig_1.png)

Reaction I: $\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3}$; Reaction II: $\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OCH_3)CH_3}$ (the central carbon carries H, $\mathrm{CH_3}$, $\mathrm{CH_3}$ and $\mathrm{OCH_3}$); Reaction III: $\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2}$.

For each of the reactions I, II and III, give suitable reagents and conditions.

Reaction I:

Reaction II:

Reaction III: *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Reaction I** (substitution of I by OH): **aqueous sodium hydroxide** (or aqueous KOH), **heated under reflux**.

$$\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} + \mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)CH_3} + \mathrm{I^-}$$

The product is propan-2-ol (nucleophilic substitution: the hydroxide ion is the nucleophile).

**Reaction II** (substitution of I by OCH$_3$): **sodium methoxide, $\mathrm{CH_3ONa}$** (the methoxide ion $\mathrm{CH_3O^-}$ prepared from sodium and dry methanol), in **methanol, heated** (under reflux).

$$\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} + \mathrm{CH_3O^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OCH_3)CH_3} + \mathrm{I^-}$$

The product is 2-methoxypropane, an ether (nucleophilic substitution by the methoxide nucleophile).

**Reaction III** (elimination of HI): **potassium (or sodium) hydroxide dissolved in ethanol** (ethanolic KOH), **heated under reflux**.

$$\mathrm{CH_3CHICH_3} + \mathrm{OH^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{I^-}$$

The product is propene (the hydroxide ion acts as a base and removes a hydrogen from a neighbouring carbon).

The difference between I and III is the solvent: **water** favours substitution, **ethanol** favours elimination.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Benzene undergoes electrophilic substitution reaction.

(i) What is an electrophilic substitution reaction?

(ii) Give an example of an electrophilic reagent.

(iii) Explain why benzene reacts with electrophilic reagents *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** An **electrophilic substitution** is a reaction in which an **electrophile** (an electron-pair acceptor, an electron-deficient species) **replaces an atom (a hydrogen atom) of the benzene ring**. The delocalised $\pi$ system of the ring is restored at the end, so the product is still aromatic (for example $\mathrm{C_6H_6} + \mathrm{HNO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$).

**(ii)** Examples of electrophiles: the **nitronium ion, $\mathrm{NO_2^+}$** (from concentrated $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ and concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$); also $\mathrm{Cl^+}$ or $\mathrm{Br^+}$ (from $\mathrm{Cl_2}$ or $\mathrm{Br_2}$ with $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ or $\mathrm{FeBr_3}$), or a carbocation $\mathrm{R^+}$ or $\mathrm{RCO^+}$ in a Friedel-Crafts reaction.

**(iii)** The benzene ring has a **high electron density above and below the plane of the ring**, because the six $\pi$ electrons are delocalised over the six carbon atoms. This region of negative charge **attracts electron-deficient (positive) electrophiles**, and the $\pi$ electrons supply the pair of electrons that forms the new bond. (The ring then substitutes rather than adds, to keep the stability given by the delocalised ring.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Ethene is obtained on a large scale from the process of cracking in the petroleum industry.

(i) What is cracking?

(ii) Write the equation of a reaction in which ethene is obtained by cracking.

(iii) Write the equation for the reaction of ethene with the following reagents:

A: Aqueous bromine

B: Concentrated sulphuric acid *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** **Cracking** is the thermal or catalytic decomposition (breaking) of long-chain hydrocarbons (heavy fractions of crude oil) into **shorter-chain, more useful alkanes and alkenes** (conditions: a zeolite catalyst at about $500^\circ\mathrm{C}$, or steam at $700$ to $900^\circ\mathrm{C}$ without a catalyst).

**(ii)** For example, decane gives octane and ethene:

$$\mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_8H_{18}} + \mathrm{C_2H_4}$$

(C: $10 = 8 + 2$; H: $22 = 18 + 4$.) Any balanced equation giving ethene is acceptable, e.g. $\mathrm{C_{12}H_{26}} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_{10}H_{22}} + \mathrm{C_2H_4}$.

**(iii)**

**A. Aqueous bromine (bromine water):** the orange colour disappears. The bromine adds across the double bond and water also takes part, giving 2-bromoethanol:

$$\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{BrCH_2CH_2OH} + \mathrm{HBr}$$

(With bromine alone, for example dissolved in an inert solvent, the product is 1,2-dibromoethane: $\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_2BrCH_2Br}$.)

**B. Concentrated sulphuric acid** (cold): addition of $\mathrm{H{-}OSO_3H}$ across the double bond gives ethyl hydrogensulphate:

$$\mathrm{CH_2{=}CH_2} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OSO_3H}$$

(Warming with water hydrolyses it to ethanol: $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OSO_3H} + \mathrm{H_2O} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} + \mathrm{H_2SO_4}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
2-aminopropanoic acid (Alanine) is an example of an amino acid.

(i) Describe a chemical test to confirm the presence of any one of the functional groups present in 2-amino propanoic acid.

(ii) Write an equation for the synthesis of 2-aminopropanoic acid from propanoic acid stating the reagents and reaction conditions. *[4 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
2-Aminopropanoic acid is $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH}$; it contains an **amino group** ($-\mathrm{NH_2}$) and a **carboxylic acid group** ($-\mathrm{COOH}$).

**(i) Test for the carboxylic acid group.** Add a little **sodium hydrogencarbonate solution** (or solid sodium carbonate) to the amino acid: **effervescence** of carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky, shows the $-\mathrm{COOH}$ group:

$$\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH} + \mathrm{NaHCO_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COONa} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{CO_2}$$

(Alternative test for the $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group: add cold nitrous acid, $\mathrm{NaNO_2}$ + dilute HCl; **nitrogen gas** is given off: $\mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH} + \mathrm{HNO_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(OH)COOH} + \mathrm{N_2} + \mathrm{H_2O}$. Warming with ninhydrin gives a purple colour with amino acids.)

**(ii) Synthesis from propanoic acid** (two steps):

*Step 1: halogenation at the alpha carbon.* Propanoic acid is brominated with **bromine in the presence of red phosphorus** (a catalyst, which forms $\mathrm{PBr_3}$), with heating:

$$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COOH} + \mathrm{Br_2} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CHBrCOOH} + \mathrm{HBr}$$

*Step 2: substitution of Br by NH$_2$.* 2-Bromopropanoic acid is heated with an **excess of concentrated ammonia** solution (in a sealed tube):

$$\mathrm{CH_3CHBrCOOH} + 2\mathrm{NH_3} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH(NH_2)COOH} + \mathrm{NH_4Br}$$

(The excess of ammonia avoids the formation of secondary amines and neutralises the HBr formed.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Give the structure and name of the main organic product of the following reactions:

(i) $\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} + 4\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow$

Structure and name of product:

(ii) $\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + \mathrm{HCl/Sn} \rightarrow$

Structure and name of product:

(iii) $\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + \mathrm{LiAlH_4}$

Structure and name of product: *[6 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** Hofmann degradation of an amide (the product has one carbon atom fewer than the amide):

$$\mathrm{CH_3CONH_2} + \mathrm{Br_2} + 4\mathrm{KOH} \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3NH_2} + \mathrm{K_2CO_3} + 2\mathrm{KBr} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$$

Atoms: C $2 = 1 + 1$; H $5 + 4 = 9 = 5 + 4$; N 1; O $1 + 4 = 5 = 3 + 2$; K $4 = 2 + 2$; Br $2 = 2$.

Product: **$\mathrm{CH_3NH_2}$, methylamine (methanamine)**, a primary amine.

**(ii)** Reduction of the nitro group by tin and hydrochloric acid (reflux), followed by neutralisation with alkali:

$$\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + 6[\mathrm{H}] \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$$

(in the acid medium the amine is formed as $\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_3^+Cl^-}$: $\mathrm{C_6H_5NO_2} + 3\mathrm{Sn} + 7\mathrm{H^+} \rightarrow \mathrm{C_6H_5NH_3^+} + 3\mathrm{Sn^{2+}} + 2\mathrm{H_2O}$; sodium hydroxide then liberates the free amine).

Product: **$\mathrm{C_6H_5NH_2}$, phenylamine (aniline)**: a benzene ring carrying an $-\mathrm{NH_2}$ group.

**(iii)** Lithium tetrahydridoaluminate(III), $\mathrm{LiAlH_4}$, in dry ether, reduces a carboxylic acid to the primary alcohol (then dilute acid or water is added):

$$\mathrm{CH_3COOH} + 4[\mathrm{H}] \rightarrow \mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH} + \mathrm{H_2O}$$

Product: **$\mathrm{CH_3CH_2OH}$, ethanol**.
